D005-D015_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling really low for a long time now… I’d say at least six months. It’s gotten worse over the last couple of months. I drag myself out of bed at 4 a.m. for my bus route, but I’m exhausted before I even start. Nothing feels enjoyable anymore—not driving, not watching the game, not even spending time with my wife or grandkids. I feel guilty all the time, like I’ve failed my family and don’t deserve them.

About two months ago, on top of feeling so down, I started getting these strange ideas. I became convinced I had some kind of special calling, like I’d been chosen to “save” people on my route, that I had powers to protect them from accidents. It sounds odd even as I say it, but it feels real in the moment.

Around the same time, I began smelling smoke or rotting meat when no one else could smell anything—on the bus, at home, even in bed. Those smells and those beliefs only happen when I’m in this really dark mood; when my mood lifts a bit for a day or two, that stuff fades too.
D005-D015_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D005-D015_h001.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h002.question:
It started about three months ago with feeling really down, but in the last two months it’s gotten much worse and…stranger. I wake up already exhausted and heavy, like there’s no point to getting out of bed, but I force myself because I have patients booked. I used to like my job, chatting with people while I cleaned their teeth. Now I feel numb and on autopilot, and I’m constantly thinking my patients would be better off with someone else. I feel worthless, like a burden to my husband.

Since this really deep sadness started, I’ve also become convinced people at work are watching me and trying to get me fired—like the front desk staff are reporting everything I do, and even cameras in the office are focused on me. I know it sounds odd, but it feels so real. At home, sometimes I suddenly get this strong taste in my mouth, like metal or chemicals, when I’m just sitting there and not eating anything. It makes me think someone’s poisoning my food or water.

These things only happen when I’m in this really low, hopeless state. Before this depressive slump, I never experienced anything like that.
D005-D015_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D005-D015_h002.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h003.question:

About two months ago, in the middle of feeling like this, other stuff started. I began to think maybe I’m not just some regular cop—that I’ve been chosen somehow, like I have a special mission to cleanse the city, almost like I’m above the law. On night shifts I see shadows that look like people standing in alleys or on rooftops, watching me, glowing a bit around the edges, but when I get closer there’s nothing there. 

Those beliefs and visions only happen when I’m in this dark mood. When, very briefly, I feel a little less depressed, they fade too.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

At the same time, I sometimes feel things crawling under my skin or brushing my arms when there’s nothing there. D005-D015_h008.question:

Sometimes when people move my arms or position me—like when my husband nudges me to sit up in bed—I just kind of stay in that position, stiff, even though it feels strange, and I don’t really care.

These thoughts and weird body stuff only happen when I’m in this deep dark mood; they weren’t there before all this depression started.

A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

I feel like a burden, like there’s no point in me being here.

Lately I’ve become convinced there’s something terribly wrong inside my body. I keep telling the nurses my insides are rotting, that my organs are decaying, even though all the tests come back “normal.” It feels very real to me. Sometimes I smell this awful, rotten odor, like something dead, but no one else can smell it. It makes me certain I’m decomposing from the inside.

The staff say I occasionally act “silly,” like making little jokes in a childish way or giggling at inappropriate times, but it’s not because I’m happy. It’s almost nervous, out of place. These strange beliefs and smells only started after I sank into this deep sadness and have only been there while I’ve been this depressed. Before I got this low, I didn’t have any of these experiences.
D005-D015_h023.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h023.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h024.question:
For about six months now, I’ve been in a really dark place. I wake up dreading the day, can’t find the energy to show houses, and I’ve been canceling on clients because I just don’t care anymore. I used to love staging homes and talking to people, but now I feel completely worthless, like a total failure since my divorce. My sleep is all over the place, my appetite’s dropped, and some mornings I just lie there thinking everyone would be better off without me.

About three months ago, on top of that, I started feeling like people were out to get me. I’m convinced my coworkers are tracking me, that there are hidden cameras in the properties I show, and that someone from the agency is trying to ruin my reputation. I hear this man’s voice, very clear, telling me I’m a fraud and that they’re watching me. It only happens when my mood is at its worst. Sometimes when I’m anxious, I catch myself rubbing and tapping my fingers over and over in the same pattern without meaning to, and it’s hard to stop once I start.

D005-D015_h025.question:
I’ve felt like I’ve been in a hole for around four months now, maybe a bit longer. It started with just feeling low and exhausted all the time, like I’m walking through mud. I used to handle long shifts fine, but now even getting out of bed for work feels pointless. I’ve lost interest in pretty much everything—gym, hanging out with friends, even gaming. My appetite’s off and I’ve lost some weight. I just feel worthless, like I’m failing as a medic and as a person, and I keep thinking everyone would be better off if I weren’t around, though I haven’t made any plans.

About three months ago, when the mood got really bad, I started noticing weird things. Radio calls or people talking at the station feel like they’re secretly about me—like they’re judging how badly I’m doing. Sometimes I hear a man’s voice, clear as day, telling me I’m useless or that I messed up a call, but no one else hears it. At work or at home I’ll catch myself rubbing my hands together over and over or tapping my fingers in the same pattern without really meaning to. When my mood slightly lifts for a day or two, the voice and those “messages” from the radio seem to fade, then they come back when the depression crashes in again.

A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h025.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
